definitions.definition: A source, situation, or act with potential for harm in terms of human injury or ill health, property damage, or environmental damage.
The combination of the probability (likelihood) of occurrence of a hazardous event and the severity of injury, ill health, or damage that could result from the event.
Risk remaining after safety controls and mitigation measures have been applied. Formula: Rr = Ri × (1 - ε), where ε is control efficiency.
An unplanned event that did not result in injury, illness, or damage but had the potential to do so. Also called 'close call', 'dangerous occurrence', or 'near-hit'.
A work-related injury or illness that results in at least one day away from work beyond the day of the incident.
TRIR = (Number of recordable incidents × 200,000) / Total hours worked. Measures frequency of OSHA recordable injuries per 100 full-time employees.
The right and responsibility of any employee or contractor to stop work when they observe or suspect a condition that poses an imminent threat to life, health, or the environment.
A formal documented system to control certain types of work that are potentially hazardous. Ensures that proper authorization, planning, and controls are in place before work begins.
The fundamental reason(s) for the occurrence of a problem that, if corrected, would prevent recurrence. Methods include 5-Why, Fault Tree Analysis, and Fishbone (Ishikawa) diagrams.

Corrective and Preventive Action. A system for investigating nonconformities, identifying root causes, and implementing actions to prevent recurrence (corrective) and prevent future issues (preventive).
The average airborne concentration of a substance over an 8-hour workday. Formula: TWA = Σ(Ci × Ti) / 8, where Ci is concentration and Ti is duration in hours.
The minimum concentration of a flammable gas or vapour in air that is capable of igniting and exploding. Concentrations at or above 10% LEL require immediate action.
